question: Synapse is the point at which a nerve impulse passes _____.

options.text: from one neuron to the next
from the brain to the spinal cord
from one epithelial cell to another
from one endocrine gland to another

solution:
The correct answer is __**from one neuron to the next**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **synapse** is a junction where a nerve impulse passes from one neuron to the next.
 
• The process involves the release of neurotransmitters from the presynaptic neuron, which then cross the synaptic cleft and bind to receptors on the postsynaptic neuron.
 
• This mechanism is essential for communication between neurons, allowing for the transmission of signals throughout the nervous system.
 
• Synapses play a critical role in the functioning of neural networks and are involved in various physiological processes, including learning and memory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **synapse** was coined by Sir Charles Sherrington in 1897.
 
• There are two main types of synapses: **chemical synapses** and **electrical synapses**.
 
• In **chemical synapses**, neurotransmitters are released from the presynaptic neuron and bind to receptors on the postsynaptic neuron.
 
• In **electrical synapses**, ions flow directly between cells through gap junctions, allowing for faster transmission of signals.
 
• Disruptions in synaptic function can lead to neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, epilepsy, and depression.
